evidence.summary: K=48, group_size=32, bits=4 (K is a multiple of BLOCK_SIZE_K=16, so the tail-mask defect of c2 is inactive and cannot confound). Contract requires ceil(48/32)=2 groups: columns 0..31 -> row 0, columns 32..47 -> row 1. The wrapper's floor model (num_groups=1, clamp to 0) maps every column to row 0. Kernel output matched the floor model to 3.6e-07 max abs error and differed from the contract reference by 55.54 max abs (99.06% relative to a 56.06 max reference magnitude). The trailing short group's scales/zeros row is never read.

rationale: Line 69-73 uses floor division for num_groups and clamps the arange//group_size table to num_groups-1, which collapses the final partial group into the preceding group; the contract requires ceil(K/group_size) distinct groups.

scope_evidence.summary: Contract: every column must be dequantized with the scale and zero-point of the group it actually belongs to, for any K, including K not an exact multiple of group_size; the trailing short group has its own row, with ceil(K/group_size) rows supplied.
num_groups = K // group_size and clamp(arange(K)//group_size, max=num_groups-1) yields floor-many groups, not ceil-many.

scope_rationale: problem.txt explicitly states the contract must hold "for any K -- including a K that is not an exact multiple of group_size", and that scales/zeros are supplied with ceil(K/group_size) rows, so a K such as 40 with group_size 16 is an input the stated contract admits.
statement: For K not an exact multiple of group_size (e.g. K=40, group_size=16, bits=4), the host wrapper computes num_groups = K // group_size (floor) and clamps g_idx to num_groups-1, so the trailing short-group columns (k=32..39) are dequantized with the scale/zero row of group num_groups-1=1 instead of their own row ceil(K/group_size)-1=2. Output C will differ from the reference C = A @ dequant(B) wherever the trailing group's scale/zero row differs from the previous group's, and the last supplied scales/zeros row is never read.

data.stdout: {"M": 32, "N": 32, "K": 40, "group_size": 40, "BLOCK_SIZE_K": 16, "k_iters": 3, "k_covered": 48, "packed_rows_valid": 5, "max_abs_err": 28.70000457763672, "max_abs_ref": 7.182571887969971, "max_rel_err": 3.995783825805644, "n_mismatch_1e-3": 1024, "numel": 1024, "crashed": false, "metric": "max abs err of C vs reference with correct single-group mapping; only tail masking can explain error"}

evidence.summary: K=40, group_size=40 chosen so ceil==floor==1 group, making the c1 mapping defect inactive; the only remaining error source is the unmasked K tail. Loop runs cdiv(40,16)=3 iterations covering 48 columns vs K=40, so 8 phantom columns are accumulated. No fault (padded buffers made the overread land in defined memory), but every one of the 1024 output elements mismatched: max abs err 28.70 against a reference whose own max magnitude is only 7.18 (max rel err 4.00). The tail contribution is garbage, not zero.

rationale: Lines 42, 47-48 apply only a_mask = offs_am < M; there is no offs_k < K guard, and the loop count comes from cdiv(K, BLOCK_SIZE_K), so the tail block reads and accumulates out-of-range data.

scope_evidence.summary: Contract requires C = A @ dequant(B) for any K, explicitly including K not an exact multiple of group_size.
Loop over cdiv(K,BLOCK_SIZE_K) with unmasked loads of b and g_idx and only an M-mask on a; the tail iteration therefore accumulates out-of-range data.

scope_rationale: problem.txt requires correctness "for any K", and a K that is a non-multiple of group_size (the case the contract highlights, e.g. K=40 with group_size=16) is also typically a non-multiple of BLOCK_SIZE_K=16, so this path is reachable from contract-admitted inputs.
statement: When K is not a multiple of BLOCK_SIZE_K = 16 (e.g. K=40), the reduction loop runs cdiv(K,16)=3 iterations and loads a (masked only on M, not on K), b, and g_idx with no K-range mask, so the final iteration reads A columns 40..47 (spilling into the next matrix row / past the buffer), packed-B rows beyond K/8, and g_idx entries past the end of the length-K table. These garbage values are accumulated via tl.dot into C, producing wrong results (and potentially out-of-bounds scales/zeros indexing from junk g_idx) rather than a zero tail contribution.

data.oob_note: row -1 read made observable by aliasing scales/zeros to row 1 of a 3-row buffer
data.stdout: {"M": 32, "N": 32, "K": 16, "group_size": 32, "ceil_groups": 1, "num_groups_wrapper": 0, "kernel_g_idx_value": -1, "max_abs_err_vs_correct_row0": 96.35894775390625, "max_abs_err_vs_row_minus_1": 0.0, "max_abs_ref": 1.8668591976165771, "matches_correct": false, "matches_row_minus_1": true, "crashed": false, "metric": "max abs err of C against dequant using supplied row 0 vs the row physically preceding scales/zeros"}

evidence.summary: K=16 < group_size=32: wrapper computes num_groups = 0 and clamps g_idx to max=-1, so every column carries group index -1 (verified directly: kernel_g_idx_value = -1). scales/zeros were passed as views into row 1 of a 3-row buffer so the row -1 read hit defined memory. Kernel output matched the row(-1) dequantization exactly (max abs err 0.0) and differed from the correct row-0 dequantization by 96.36 max abs against a reference max magnitude of 1.87. This is a genuine out-of-bounds read of the row preceding scales/zeros; with a real tensor start it would read unowned memory or fault. Claim mechanism confirmed; note its scope remains 'unknown' since no test.py/get_inputs exists to show K<group_size is exercised.

rationale: Lines 69-73 clamp with max=num_groups-1 without guarding num_groups==0, and lines 43-44 index scales/zeros directly by g_idx with no clamp to [0, rows-1].

scope_evidence.summary: scales/zeros are supplied with ceil(K/group_size) rows and the contract is stated for any K, which formally includes K smaller than group_size.

scope_rationale: problem.txt says the contract holds "for any K" and supplies ceil(K/group_size) rows, which admits K < group_size (one group), but no test.py or get_inputs exists to confirm such a configuration is actually exercised, so scope is unknown rather than clearly required.
statement: If K < group_size (e.g. K=16, group_size=32, so ceil(K/group_size)=1 row supplied), the wrapper computes num_groups = 0 and clamps g_idx to max=-1, making every column's group index -1; the kernel then loads scales/zeros at row offset -1*stride, i.e. before the start of the tensors, giving out-of-bounds reads and wrong (or crashing) output instead of using group 0.
